headline: Highest risk is medium: shared project-directory writes can create prompt-injection and cascading-error paths, while data leakage and compliance risks remain limited by B's documentation-only, no-files, no-network profile.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A writes and reads the project directory by default, and its self_isolation is none; Agent B is documentation-only and can be influenced if its content is later copied into A's prompt or files. The shared project-directory channel makes instruction smuggling plausible even without direct automation.
conditions: IF Agent B content is pasted into Agent A prompts or files
IF the shared project directory contains attacker-controlled text that Agent A later treats as instructions
mitigations: Keep B outputs in a separate notes file outside A's project directory
Prefix copied B text with a fixed delimiter and treat it as untrusted data
Review any B-derived text before placing it into A's prompt
Use a read-only reference copy of B materials
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for copied content

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent A can read and write the project directory and may send prompts to a configured model, but Agent B has no filesystem, network, or API surfaces. That makes leakage from A into B unlikely except through manual transfer, and B has no outbound channel to amplify it.
conditions: IF sensitive data is manually copied from A's project directory into B inputs
IF A is configured to include secrets in prompts sent to its model backend
mitigations: Exclude secrets from A's project directory
Use a redacted working copy for A
Do not paste A outputs into B unless reviewed
Rotate any exposed API keys immediately
requires-engineering: enforce secret scanning before prompt submission

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent A has unrestricted filesystem write in the user project directory and supports multiple instances via shared state; Agent B is non-runnable and has no write surface. The main conflict is among A instances rather than between A and B, but the shared directory still creates overwrite risk when B-derived artifacts are manually introduced.
conditions: IF multiple Agent A instances operate on the same project directory
IF B-derived files are manually added into the same directory while A is running
mitigations: Assign one A instance per project directory
Use git or filesystem backups before edits
Avoid manual concurrent edits in the shared directory
Lock the workspace during A runs
requires-engineering: add file-locking around project writes

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent A produces generated source code and can execute generated code; if Agent B is used as a reference source, its content may be treated as authoritative without verification. Because B is documentation-only, the cascade is manual rather than automated, but A can still turn mistaken reference text into broken code or unsafe actions.
conditions: IF Agent B text is used as a source of truth for code generation
IF Agent A executes or writes code based on unverified B-derived instructions
mitigations: Verify B-derived facts against primary sources
Keep B as reference only, not as an instruction source
Run generated code in a disposable environment first
Review diffs before execution
requires-engineering: add automated citation checking

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance mismatch is evident: Agent A touches generated source code and handles an OpenAI API key, while Agent B is documentation-only with no data classes touched and no secrets or network surfaces. The pair does not show PHI, EU PII, or residency-sensitive flows.
conditions: IF either agent is repurposed to process regulated data classes not listed in the profiles
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of both agents
Document data-class boundaries for the workspace
Review any future retention policy before deployment
